name: Adiantum

priority: Full mature frond outline: elongate/triangular versus horseshoe fan.
Location of major pinna attachment: along extended rachis versus radiating near stipe apex.
Fertile pinnule margin: false indusium is shared, not a species separator.
study_strategy.warning: A. pedatum is not Texas-native under current Kew; do not confuse generic nursery/common-name use with local occurrence.
shared_traits: Both are rhizomatous ferns with glossy dark stipes and fan- or wedge-shaped pinnules.
Both bear marginal sori under folded pinnule margins (false indusia), and reproduce by spores rather than seeds.

quick_split: A. capillus-veneris — Central Texas seep/cliff species with elongate branching fronds and fan-shaped pinnules.
A. pedatum — northern/eastern species with fanlike radiating pinnae; nonlocal comparison only.

look_here_first: Trace a complete mature frond: A. capillus-veneris has an elongated, repeatedly branched blade; A. pedatum has major pinnae radiating near the stipe tip into a horseshoe-shaped fan. Both have black stalks and folded fertile margins.

quick_key.if: Frond branches lengthwise along an extended rachis
Major pinnae radiate near the distal stipe into a horseshoe fan
